text.p: Following are some major events to have occurred on August 15 in history:
1057 - Macbeth, King of Scotland whose life was the basis for Shakespeare's play, was killed by Malcolm Canmore at Lumphanan, near Aberdeen.
1534 - The Society of Jesus (Jesuits) was founded in Paris by St Ignatius of Loyola.
1537 - Spanish conquistador Juan de Salazar founded Nuestra Senora Santa Maria de la Asuncion, now the capital of Paraguay.
1684 - Truce of Ratisbon was signed between Holy Roman Empire and France, guaranteeing peace for 20 years.
1688 - Frederick William, King of Prussia 1713-40 who revolutionised the country's administration, born.
1769 - Napoleon Bonaparte, French military leader and emperor, born in Ajaccio, Corsica. After his defeat in 1815 by Wellington at Waterloo, he was banished to St Helena where he died.
1771 - Sir Walter Scott, Scottish author, born. Wrote many historical romances including "Guy Mannering", "Ivanhoe" and "Heart of Midlothian".
1807 - Francois Paul Jules Grevy, president of France 1879-87 during the Third Republic, born.
1834 - British parliament passed an act allowing for the colonisation of South Australia.
1867 - Second Reform Act in Britain extends suffrage to householders and land owners, nearly doubling the electorate.
1879 - Ethel Barrymore, U.S. stage and screen actress and acknowledged First Lady of the American Theatre, born in Philadelphia as Ethel Blythe.
1888 - T.E. (Thomas Edward) Lawrence, British adventurer, writer, archaeologist and soldier, born. Known as "Lawrence of Arabia" after leading the Arab revolt against the Turks 1917-18.
1914 - The Panama Canal opened with passage of the vessel Ancon, although it was not formally inaugurated until July 1920.
1917 - Deposed Russian Tsar Nicholas II and family were moved from their residence at Tsarskoe Selo to further imprisonment in Siberia.
1917 - Jack Lynch, Irish statesman and prime minister 1966-1973 and 1977-1979, born. Became the Irish Republic's fifth prime minister in 1966 as leader of the Fianna Fail (Soldiers of Destiny) party.
1918 - The United States severed diplomatic relations with Russia in wake of Bolshevik takeover.
1924 - Robert Bolt, British playwright, screenwriter and director, born. Noted for his stage play "A Man For All Seasons" and his scripts for the films "Lawrence of Arabia" and "Dr Zhivago".
1925 - Oscar Peterson, Canadian jazz pianist and composer, born. Achieved international fame with his touring "Jazz at the Philharmonic".
1930 - Tom Mboya, Kenyan politician and leader in the country's struggle for independence, born.
1935 - Wiley Post, American aviator, killed in a plane crash in Alaska along with his passenger, American humourist Will Rogers.
1944 - U.S. Seventh Army began Operation Dragoon, a landing on the French Riviera to open up a second front after the Normandy landings of June.
1945 - Millions worldwide celebrated VJ (Victory in Japan) Day, the day after it was announced the Japanese had surrendered.
1947 - The Indian Independence Bill came into force, setting up the two independent states of India and Pakistan.
1948 - South Korea became independent and was formally proclaimed as the Republic of Korea, with Syngman Rhee as first president.
1950 - An earthquake measuring about 8.7 on the Richter scale struck Assam, killing over 1,000.
1950 - Princess Anne, second child and only daughter of Britain's Queen Elisabeth, born. Has won wide acclaim as a no-nonsense campaigner for international charities.
1960 - Republic of the Congo is proclaimed an independent nation within the French Community.
1965 - Crowd of 55,600 attended a Beatles concert at Shea Stadium, New York, creating world attendance and revenue records for a pop concert.
1969 - The legendary Woodstock Music and Arts Fair began in Bethel, New York.
1971 - Bahrain became a separate independent state.
1974 - The wife of South Korean President Park Chung-Hee was shot dead by an assassin in an attempt on Park's life. Park himself was assassinated in October 1979.
1975 - The president of Bangladesh, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, was killed by army officers in a dawn coup which overthrew his government.
1979 - Two Soviet Aeroflot airliners collided in mid-air over Ukraine, killing 173.
1990 - President Mikhail Gorbachev restored Soviet citizenship to Nobel prize-winning author Alexander Solzhenitsyn, expelled to the West in 1974 for his harrowing novels attacking Stalinism.
1994 - Sudanese security agents, tipped off by Paris, captured wanted international guerrilla Illich Ramirez Sanchez, known as "Carlos the Jackal".
1995 - Fifty years after World War Two ended in the Pacific, Japan made its first clear-cut apology for the country's wartime actions.
1996 - Senior Bosnian officials signed an agreement to fully form the country's Moslem-Croat Federation and dismantle the self-styled Bosnian Croat republic of Herceg-Bosna.
